item_description_text: A mountain is a very tall natural landform that rises high above the land around it, making it a type of place on Earth. Mountains formed billions of years ago when huge pieces of the Earth slowly pushed together or when volcanoes built up layers of rock, and no person made them—they come from natural forces deep inside the planet. They are found all over the world and often have rocky sides, plants, or snowy tops, with the very top called a peak. Mountains are special because they are some of the highest places on Earth, can be very cold at the top, and help create rivers and weather, and even though they can look different—some sharp, some round—they are all known for being much taller than the land nearby.
